p1: [low, ominous] Nine hikers cut their tent open... [whispers] from the inside... [low] and ran into the snow without boots.
[low] Russia's Ural Mountains. February, nineteen fifty-nine.
[low] Ten skiers set out. One fell sick and turned back. [low, ominous] He was the only one who came home.
[low] The other nine camped on a slope the Mansi people call... [whispers] Dead Mountain.
[low, tense] Weeks later, searchers found the tent. [whispers] Their boots were still inside.
[low] The first bodies lay near the trees, by a small fire. [low, cold] Some in just their underwear.
[low, tense] The last four weren't found... [whispers] until months later.
[low, ominous] One had a fractured skull. Two, crushed chests. [whispers] Their clothes had traces of radiation.
[low, cold] The Soviet verdict: a compelling natural force.
[low] In twenty nineteen, Russia reopened the case and blamed an avalanche.
[low, tense] But what made nine people cut their way out... [whispers] into the dark? [low, ominous] Nobody knows for sure.
